newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nervous German DAX drops 0.5 pct amid EMU talk.
newsitem.headline: Nervous German DAX drops 0.5 pct amid EMU talk.

text.p: German shares eased on Friday from Thursday's record levels as poor overnight performances in Japan and the U.S. combined with unsubstantiated talk of a delay to monetary union to put the market under pressure.
The 30-share DAX index dropped 17.08 points, or 0.5 percent, to 3,259.64 in bourse trade.

Prices dropped rapidly after a faintly weak start as rumours spread that Germany was poised to announce a delayed start for European Economic and Monetary union (EMU), triggering fears for exporters' earnings.
The decline halted after the Bundesbank and the Finance Ministry denied any such plans, but the thinly-traded market lacked impetus for another advance, dealers said.
Nonetheless, a bullish mood was still underpinning German shares, amid expectations that more earnings upgrades are to come on the back of the dollar's dramatic gains this year.

"The EMU issue should be over for the moment but it hasn't stopped people taking profits today. But there is still more upside in this market and we should see that next week," a dealer at a Bavarian bank said.
The declines were spread across the board, with most blue chip shares under pressure.

Volkswagen however rose nine marks to 818 marks after the carmaker said on Thursday that sales in January rose 18 percent and it expected to maintain its world market share in 1997 despite difficult industry conditions.
The other outperformer was retail group Metro, which ended up four percent at 148 marks after breaking above a key technical barrier, pushing it briefly over to an all-time high of 148.50 marks.
